title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Weekly POC sync to review the reliability incident on 2026-03-31 where the pilot saw increased 5xxs and timeouts under sustained load. Redwood presented initial traces and a hypothesis (bursting CPU on inference nodes + KV cache thrash + client-side retry storms). Discussed short-term mitigations (rate limiting, backoff tuning, temporary capacity bump) and mid-term fixes (autoscale tuning, request routing to quieter regions, improved cache priming). Agreed on concrete next steps: share full trace bundle, run controlled retry & rate-limit tests, and schedule capacity tuning call next week.
action_items: Sofia (Redwood) : Share zipped request traces and 5xx logs by 2026-04-02
Ethan (Redwood SE) : Run a controlled replay of the failing traffic pattern and share JVM/PyTorch metrics by 2026-04-05
Mark (Nimbus SRE) : Run client-side retry experiments with adjusted backoff and provide results by 2026-04-04
Priya (Nimbus) : Confirm production traffic window for a temporary capacity bump by 2026-04-03
next_steps: Redwood to propose temporary rate-limiting policy and config snippet
Nimbus to run retry/backoff test and share results
Schedule capacity tuning call (Redwood SE + Nimbus SRE) for 2026-04-06
Redwood to supply an annotated trace packet and dashboard links
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-01
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE); Ethan Cole (Redwood SE); Priya Singh (Head of ML, Nimbus); Mark Reynolds (SRE, Nimbus); Aisha Omar (PM, Nimbus)

Auto-summary: Incident follow-up for increased 5xxs/timeouts seen in pilot; agree on mitigations and next steps.

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll do a quick run through of the incident from yesterday and then outline steps. Ethan will lead on the traces.
[00:22] Ethan (Redwood SE): Yeah hi, hey. So quick context — 03/31 around 14:12 UTC we saw a spike in 5xxs and elevated latencies, mostly on the inference tier. I've got a compressed trace bundle in the shared drive (link posted in chat).
[00:45] Priya (Customer): Thanks, uh, we saw client-side retries amplify things maybe? Mark, you had some graphs?
[01:10] Mark (Customer SRE): Yeah, um, on our side we saw retry storms kick in around the same time, and overall qps increased by about 40% during the window. We also noticed some nodes reporting higher CPU and repeated KV cache misses.
[01:35] Ethan: Right so first pass — hypothesis is threefold: 1) bursty traffic caused the kernel to saturate for a subset of GPUs leading to longer queues; 2) KV cache thrash caused more cold-started decoding which bumps latencies; 3) client retry behavior without jitter amplified transient errors into sustained 5xxs.
[02:10] Aisha (Customer PM): Can you explain KV cache thrash in plain terms? We sometimes get lost in infra words.
[02:25] Ethan: Sure — it's basically the model key-value cache that stores previous tokens for faster decoding. If the cache is being evicted frequently because requests are to many different contexts, the runtime has to re-populate the cache which costs time, so it shows up as latency spikes. Sometimes transcripts autoparses that as "K V" which is why it's odd.
[03:00] Sofia: There's also a note — some of the 5xxs correlate with our autoscaler not spinning up additional Dedicated instances fast enough, likely due to tuning conservative cool-down windows. That plus retry storms equals the visible outage.
[03:30] Priya: Is this more Dedicated config or a code/runtime bug?
[03:45] Ethan: We're leaning toward config + workload mismatch. No evidence of a fatal runtime bug in the core engine — the traces show queued requests and timeouts, not kernel panics. But we did see occasional GPU OOMs on one older node which is flagged.
[04:10] Mark: The OOMs were small bursts, maybe related to a slightly longer sequence length in a fraction of requests. We'll flag those request IDs.
[04:35] Ethan: Good — those IDs will help. For immediate mitigation we recommend three items: 1) apply client-side backoff with jitter and cap retries (example snippet shared), 2) temporary soft rate-limit at the Redwood front-door for the pilot tenant to flatten bursts, and 3) bump reserved Dedicated capacity for the next 24-48 hours while we tune autoscale.
[05:15] Priya: For the cap retries, what number? Our current SDK retries up to 5 times with no jitter.
[05:30] Sofia: We usually recommend 2-3 retries with exponential backoff and jitter, and a max total retry time of 5-10s for chat/generation loops. We'll send a sample config.
[06:00] Aisha: About rate-limiting — is that tenant-level or route-level? We need per-route for embeddings vs chat.
[06:20] Ethan: Good call — we can do per-route token-based limits. For the pilot we suggest route-level soft caps: slightly lower for embedding-heavy routes and higher for chat. We'll share a config example.
[07:00] Priya: You mentioned autoscaler cooldowns were conservative — can you give numbers?
[07:20] Ethan: Current config uses a 3-minute scale-up cool-down and 10-minute scale-down window. For this workload we recommend lowering scale-up cool-down to 60s and allowing quicker short-lived bursts to be served. Also adjust the scale trigger threshold from 70% GPU to 55% for pilot nodes.
[07:55] Mark: Any impact on cost if we change that? We need to know economics — short-term bump is fine for incident recovery.
[08:15] Sofia: There will be a cost impact for the temp bump, but small relative to preventing user-impact. We'll provide an estimate once Ethan runs the replay.
[08:35] Speaker 1: (inaudible) we should also consider routing to a secondary region if capacity there is idle.
[08:50] Ethan: Yeah, smart routing — we did see that us-west had spare capacity. We can failover some requests to us-west with region-aware routing, but that has implications for data residency.
[09:20] Priya: Data residency is a blocker for some segments — we need to keep EU requests in EU. This pilot is EU-first so routing is limited.
[09:40] Ethan: Understood — we'll keep routing suggestions EU-local. Another thing: cache priming. If you can send a set of top contexts we can pre-warm KV cache to reduce cold misses.
[10:05] Priya: We'll export the top 200 contexts from the last week and share.
[10:20] Mark: On the logs — what format do you need? We can export request IDs and full traces.
[10:35] Sofia: The trace bundle we need is the gzipped request traces CSV plus the inference node metrics (GPU util, CPU, mem) for the window. Ethan put a checklist in the chat.
[11:00] Aisha: About retries — we already have client changes mid-week; will that risk more instability?
[11:15] Ethan: If done with exponential backoff + jitter and lower max retries it's stabilizing. The issue is synchronous retries without jitter.
[11:35] Priya: Is this a common pattern with other vendors? Our infra team observed similar behavior in a previous Bedrock pilot.
[11:50] Sofia: Yes, many teams run into that — it's the retry storm problem. We also add server-side mitigation because you can't control all SDKs.
[12:10] Ethan: For server-side we can throttle per-tenant QPS and enforce queuing with a 429 that carries a Retry-After header, but we prefer to avoid hard rejects if possible. Soft throttles are friendlier.
[12:40] Mark: Can Redwood push a temporary rule just for the pilot tenant?
[12:50] Sofia: Yep we can. It'd be a config change; low risk. We'll propose the config by tomorrow.
[13:10] Priya: You mentioned OOMs on older nodes — are those candidates for replacement?
[13:25] Ethan: Yes, we recommend cordoning older hardware and migrating workloads off them for the pilot. We'll mark those nodes.
[13:45] Aisha: How long to migrate?
[13:55] Ethan: For the pilot we can do a rolling cordon over 2 hours with minimal disruption if rate-limits are in place.
[14:10] Sofia: Quick reminder — we also need to solidify success criteria for the pilot after remediation: <100 5xxs per day, p95 latency under 500ms for chat, and no user-facing errors for critical routes. Priya, does that align with your goals?
[14:35] Priya: Yeah, p95 under 500ms is ideal. We'll accept a slightly higher embedding latency but keep failures zero.
[15:00] Ethan: Ok we'll put those targets in the doc. Now on benchmarks: I'll run a deterministic replay of the 03/31 traffic with varying retry configs and an autoscale tweak. Expect results by EOD Monday.
[15:25] Mark: When you replay, can you also vary sequence length distribution? We saw some long sequences in 10% of requests.
[15:40] Ethan: Yep we'll include that.
[16:00] Priya: Any security/compliance impacts with trace sharing? We need sanitized traces.
[16:15] Sofia: We recommend removing PII and we'll sign the NDA addendum for traces if needed. The traces are mostly request IDs, latencies, and metric counters.
[16:35] Aisha: On instrumentation — can Redwood add a per-request header to help trace routing?
[16:45] Ethan: Definitely, we can ask you to add X-Client-Request-Id or similar; that will make correlation easier.
[17:10] Speaker 2 (customer): the auto transcript says something about "KV cache prime" — can you show how to do that?
[17:25] Ethan: We'll provide a script to prime the top contexts — it's basically a sequence of warm requests that populate the cache. We'll share in the repo.
[18:00] Sofia: Let's recap next steps — I'll go first. Redwood will share the full trace bundle and a proposed rate-limiting config by 2026-04-02. Ethan will run replay tests and post results by 2026-04-05. Nimbus will run client retry experiments by 2026-04-04. We'll schedule a capacity tuning call for 2026-04-06.
[18:30] Priya: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? Not really. We'll gather top contexts and sanitized traces.
[19:00] Aisha: One last Q — if the temporary bump works, how quickly can you scale down? We don't want long-term costs.
[19:15] Ethan: We can set a 24-48 hour window and then reassess after the replay and tuning. We'll automate scale-down after the window if metrics look stable.
[19:40] Mark: For follow-up, can we get a dashboard link for real-time tail errors?
[19:55] Sofia: Yes will share Grafana link with a read-only view.
[20:10] Priya: ok thanks everyone.
[20:20] Sofia: Thanks all — we'll follow up in chat and see you next week.

End of transcript.
